info.name: Zenzy API (1.0.0)
info.description:
Every operation of the Zenzy server, generated from docs/openapi.yaml.

**Start here**
1. Open the collection > Variables and set `username` (a free name) and `email` (an inbox you can read).
2. Send Auth > "Sign-up step 1", copy the 6-digit code from the e-mail into the variable `code`, send "Sign-up step 2".
   The tokens are stored automatically and every other request uses them. Later, "Sign in" does the same.
3. Requests that create something (event, shop, post, chat) store its id for the requests after them.

Access tokens live 15 minutes: send Auth > "Exchange a refresh token" (or "Sign in") when requests start answering 401.
The Admin folder needs an ADMIN account in `admin_username` / `admin_password`.
The server limits how often some routes may be called (429 with `retry_after`), so do not run the collection in a loop.

variable.description: Server address without /v1. Local server: http://127.0.0.1:3100
Account used by the collection (3-30: a-z 0-9 _ .). Change it to a name that is free
A real inbox of yours: the 6-digit sign-up code is sent here
The 6-digit code from the sign-up e-mail (filled automatically on a local server)
The 6-digit code from the password-reset e-mail (filled automatically on a local server)
A Google ID token, only for POST /auth/google
Filled by register/verify, login and refresh
An ADMIN account, only for the Admin folder
Another user: filled by GET /users (first result), or paste an id
Centre used by the map, events and NEARBY feed requests
Filled by POST /events (the event chat) or POST /conversations

request.description:
Set the collection variables `username` and `email` first. On the deployed server the 6-digit code arrives by e-mail: copy it into the variable `code`, then send "verify".

Validates the data and e-mails a 6-digit code (valid 15 minutes). No account exists until `POST /auth/register/verify`. Registering again with the same e-mail replaces the pending sign-up. At most 5 sign-ups per IP every 15 minutes.

Errors:
- 400: `INVALID_INPUT` (the message lists the fields)
- 409: `USERNAME_TAKEN` or `EMAIL_TAKEN`
- 429: `TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `BROWSING_PAUSED` or `LOCATION_JUMP`
- 503: `MAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED`

request.description:
Wrong passwords in a row lock the account: 5 = 1 minute, 10 = 5 minutes, 15 = 10 minutes (`429 ACCOUNT_LOCKED` with `retry_after`), 20 = `403 PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED` until the password is reset. Admin accounts are refused here and use `POST /admin/login`.

Errors:
- 401: `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`
- 403: `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` (message has the reason) or `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED`
- 429: `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` (with `retry_after`) or `TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS` (30 failures / 15 min per IP)

request.description:
Each refresh token works once. A token used again more than 10 seconds later is treated as stolen: every token of that sign-in is revoked (`REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`) and the user must log in again.

Errors:
- 401: `INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN` or `REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`

request.description:
Needs a real Google ID token in the variable `google_id_token`; without one the answer is 401 INVALID_GOOGLE_TOKEN.

The first time, `400 PROFILE_REQUIRED` asks for `username` and `date_of_birth`; send the same token again with them.

Errors:
- 400: `PROFILE_REQUIRED` or `INVALID_INPUT`
- 401: `INVALID_GOOGLE_TOKEN`
- 403: `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` or `ADMIN_WEB_ONLY`
- 409: `USERNAME_TAKEN`
